heading: INT. ROADSIDE MOTEL ICE MACHINE ALCOVE - NIGHT

units.text: INT. ROADSIDE MOTEL ICE MACHINE ALCOVE - NIGHT
A concrete nook under a buzzing sodium lamp.
A rusted ice machine hums, its chute dripping.
Behind it, a stairwell to a second-floor gallery of doors.
Moths bomb the light.
DARNELL WITHERSPOON, thirties, a trucker in a stained jacket, fills a plastic bucket at the chute while his sister, ODESSA WITHERSPOON-LU, thirties, leans on the railing with a cigarette.
Between them, a third figure: LITTLE MILO WITHERSPOON, nine, Darnell's son, who sits on the bottom stair with a handheld game, eyes down.
The machine coughs.
A block of ice crashes into the bin and, as Darnell leans in, he pulls back his hand and stares at the bucket.
Something dark swirls in the meltwater, slow as smoke.
Odessa takes a drag and looks at the sky.
Milo, absorbed in his game, lifts his foot onto the second step, and from the gallery above comes the creak of a door none of them heard open.
Darnell tips the bucket out onto the pavement.
The water runs black and then clear.
Milo. Come here.
units.name: DARNELL

units.text: I'm on level six.
units.name: MILO

units.text: Now, bud.
units.name: DARNELL

units.text: Milo looks up.
Past his father.
Up the stairs.
His face goes slack.
Dad? Who's the lady in the window?
units.name: MILO

units.text: Odessa drops her cigarette.
Darnell does not turn around.
